common_meaning: Plural of that: referring to people or things at a distance, or already mentioned.
example: Those shoes by the door are mine.
rrgm_bridge: Those points outward to a group set apart from the speaker, in space, time or discussion.
invariant_mi: A plural demonstrative pointing to referents distant from the speaker or previously identified.

domain_entries.LIN: Demonstrative determiner and pronoun, plural of "that"; contrasts with "these".

count_condition: A plural referent that is distant or already introduced.
transfer_boundary: "Those people" can be used to distance or other a group; the pointing word can carry a judgement.

common_meaning: On or during this present day; also in the present period.
example: I have to finish the report today; young people today use phones for everything.
rrgm_bridge: Today is the present day, the one unit of time in which action can still be taken.
invariant_mi: The current day, or the present era.

domain_entries.LIN: Deictic: what "today" refers to depends on when it is said.
domain_entries.DIG: For a system without a clock, "today" has to be supplied from outside; it cannot be inferred from training alone.

count_condition: The day on which the speaker speaks, or the present age.
transfer_boundary: "Today" in a written record means the day it was written, not the day it is read. Statements about "people today" are generalisations.

common_meaning: Despite the fact that; however; nevertheless.
example: Though it was raining, we went for a walk.
rrgm_bridge: Though holds two facts together, one of which might have prevented the other, and lets both stand.
invariant_mi: Introduces a concession: a fact that runs against the main claim without cancelling it.

domain_entries.LIN: Conjunction ("though it rained") and adverb ("it was good, though").
domain_entries.FOR: Concession: both clauses are asserted; the contrast is between expectation and outcome.

count_condition: Two statements in tension, both held true.
transfer_boundary: A concession does not weaken the main claim; it admits a fact that might have been expected to.

common_meaning: To make an effort to do something; to test something to see if it works or is good; also to put someone on trial.
example: Try the new recipe; I tried to call but there was no answer.
rrgm_bridge: To try is to act without a guaranteed outcome: the effort is real whether or not it lands.
invariant_mi: To make an attempt, or to test.

domain_entries.COG: Trial and error: trying, observing, adjusting.
domain_entries.FOR: A trial run tests a method before committing to it.
domain_entries.REL: Being tried in court; and "trying" someone's patience.

count_condition: An effort or test whose outcome is uncertain.
transfer_boundary: Trying is not succeeding, and failing after trying is not the same as not trying. Being tried in court is not being found guilty.

common_meaning: Coming after the second in order; also one of three equal parts.
example: She finished third; a third of the class was absent.
rrgm_bridge: Third is the first position past a pair, where a new perspective can stand outside the two.
invariant_mi: The ordinal number corresponding to three, or one of three equal parts.

domain_entries.REL: A third party stands outside a two-sided relation and may mediate, judge or be affected.

count_condition: The position after second, or one part in three.
transfer_boundary: A third party is outside the relation, not neutral by default.

common_meaning: A settlement larger than a village and smaller than a city.
example: She grew up in a small town by the coast.
rrgm_bridge: A town is a settlement big enough to have its own centre, small enough for people to recognise each other.
invariant_mi: A populated settlement intermediate between village and city.

domain_entries.REL: Town life often means denser personal networks than in a city.
domain_entries.ECO: Towns serve as markets and service centres for surrounding areas.

count_condition: A settlement recognised locally or legally as a town.
transfer_boundary: The line between town, village and city differs by country and is sometimes legal rather than about size.

common_meaning: Reflexive and emphatic form of they; also used for a single person.
rrgm_bridge: Themselves turns the action back onto those who did it.
invariant_mi: Reflexive pronoun for a third-person plural or singular-they referent.

domain_entries.LIN: Reflexive and intensifier; "themself" is sometimes used for one person.

count_condition: A sentence in which they act on themselves, or for emphasis.
transfer_boundary: See they: pronoun choice can follow a person's own naming.

common_meaning: Money that people and businesses must pay to the government to fund public services.
example: Income tax is taken from her pay.
rrgm_bridge: Tax is the share of private income a public structure takes to keep shared services running.
invariant_mi: A compulsory payment to government, set by law.

domain_entries.ECO: Income, sales, property and other taxes; who bears a tax can differ from who pays it.
domain_entries.REL: Taxation and representation: who is taxed and who decides are long-standing political questions.

count_condition: A legally required payment to a governing authority.
transfer_boundary: Tax avoidance (legal) and tax evasion (illegal) are different. The person who hands over a tax is not always the person who bears its cost.

common_meaning: The buying and selling of goods and services; also a skilled job, especially one done with the hands; as a verb, to exchange.
example: Trade between the two countries has grown; he learned the plumbing trade.
rrgm_bridge: Trade is exchange that runs both ways, so that each side gives up something to get something else.
invariant_mi: Exchange of goods, services or skills, or a skilled occupation.

domain_entries.ECO: Trade between nations is governed by tariffs and agreements.

count_condition: An exchange between parties, or a skilled craft.
transfer_boundary: Trade benefits both sides on average but not every person in each country; some lose even when totals rise.

common_meaning: The application of scientific knowledge to practical purposes; also machines and devices built that way.
example: New technology made the factory safer.
rrgm_bridge: Technology is knowledge turned into tools, which then reshape the people who use them.
invariant_mi: Practical methods and devices derived from knowledge.

domain_entries.DIG: Computing and digital systems, often meant by "tech" today.
domain_entries.ECO: Technology changes productivity, jobs and markets.
domain_entries.REL: Who controls a technology shapes who benefits from it.

count_condition: Applied knowledge in methods or devices.
transfer_boundary: Technology is neither good nor bad by itself; its effects depend on use and access. New is not automatically better.

common_meaning: On the present or coming evening or night.
rrgm_bridge: Tonight names the coming evening, close enough to plan.
invariant_mi: The evening or night of the present day.

domain_entries.LIN: Deictic: depends on when it is said.

count_condition: The night of the day on which it is spoken.
transfer_boundary: In a written message, "tonight" means the night it was written.

common_meaning: The day after today; also the near future.
rrgm_bridge: Tomorrow is the next day, where plans and promises are placed.
invariant_mi: The day following the present day.

domain_entries.LIN: Deictic: depends on when it is said.

count_condition: The day after the speaker's present day.
transfer_boundary: "Tomorrow" in an old note means the day after it was written; "tomorrow never comes" names endless delay.

common_meaning: To go from one place to another, especially over a long distance; also the activity of doing so.
example: They travel to Japan every year.
rrgm_bridge: Travel moves a person through places, and changes what they have seen.
transfer_boundary: Seeing a place briefly is not knowing it.

common_meaning: In every part of; during the whole of.
rrgm_bridge: Throughout spreads a state over the whole of a span.
invariant_mi: In every part, or for the whole duration.
count_condition: A state covering a whole space or period.
transfer_boundary: "Throughout" claims full coverage; one gap breaks it.

common_meaning: A journey visiting several places; also a guided visit; also a series of performances in different places.
example: The band is on tour; a tour of the castle.
rrgm_bridge: A tour is a loop through several places that comes back where it started.
invariant_mi: A journey through a series of places, or a guided visit.
count_condition: A circuit of visits or performances.
transfer_boundary: A guided tour shows what the guide chooses to show.
